newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-MILAN FANS STONE TEAM BUS AFTER CUP EXIT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MILAN FANS STONE TEAM BUS AFTER CUP EXIT.

text.p: Angry AC Milan fans hurled cans and stones at their team's bus after the Italian champions were dumped out of the European Cup on Wednesday on Arrigo Sacchi's return as coach.
Groups of furious followers milled around the San Siro stadium after Milan's 2-1 Champions' League defeat by Norway's Rosenborg, preventing the team from leaving.
When the coach finally emerged from the stadium well after midnight with a police escort and the blinds pulled down, it was met by a hail of stones, cans and other objects.
The Rosenborg bus was applauded as it left.
Bottles had earlier been thrown from the terraces as the team trudged off the pitch, with the main insults reserved for goalkeeper Sebastiano Rossi and striker Marco Simone.
Some fans had also burst into the VIP hall, kicking publicity posters and shouting insults.
"I understand the fans' disappointment but they should also understand that we are not supermen," said Italian international defender Paolo Maldini afterwards. "We can also make mistakes."
That fact was not lost on the 29,000-strong crowd, who watched in dismay as a humble club, beaten 4-1 by Milan in Norway earlier, twice took the lead.
The media lashing on Thursday was as painful as Sacchi returned in defeat just as he had left Italy, whose last match under him was a 2-1 loss to Bosnia in Sarajevo.
"Sacchi gets immediate KO. Milan's a disaster," said the daily Gazzetta dello Sport in its front page headline.
"Sacchi, you're out" crowed the Corriere dello Sport.
"Milan fired," commented Tuttosport, a Turin daily whose sub-headline "The party continues" reflected its greater allegiance to triumphant champions Juventus.
"Tabarez or Sacchi, nothing changes," it added.
Uruguayan coach Oscar Washington Tabarez resigned on Sunday after Milan lost 3-2 to lowly Piacenza in the league.
Sacchi, who coached Milan to two European Cup triumphs in 1989 and 1990, handed in his notice as Italy coach and returned to Milan to try to rescue a dismal season.
The club is ninth in the league, out of European competition and also out of the domestic cup.
Sacchi, disliked by a multitude of Italians despite taking Italy to the 1994 World Cup final, escaped blame for the nightmare evening but the Milan players did not.
"Rossi brings down Milan. One mistake after the other," commented the Gazzetta dello Sport.
"It could not be the Milan of Sacchi, it was not that of Tabarez. It was just a helpless Milan, arriving at the end of a great adventure," the newspaper reported.
Milan have won four out of the last five Italian titles but this season have looked woefully out of sorts.

The defeat was the most humiliating in Europe since billionaire media mogul Silvio Berlusconi took over the club a decade ago. Milan, winners of the European Cup five times, had never before gone out of the tournament so early.
Berlusconi said the defeat was "the lowest point in our luck ...since I have been at Milan".
"I'm disappointed and saddened. But we have to learn from it and rebuild."
He said Sacchi was the ideal man for the hard job ahead.
"I need to watch, study," the coach said. "It would be wrong to make too many judgments for the lads and me.
"The will was there...other things were lacking. I don't know. We'll see. I think that you always reap what you have sown during the previous months," Sacchi added.
"Now it just remains for us to work hard."
Milan's next league match is at home to Udinese on Sunday.
